To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cyclophilin domain of Ran-binding protein 2 (RanBp2), an integral component of the nuclear pore complex, selectively modulates the activity of the ubiquitin proteasome system.

the CLD of the Ran-binding protein- 2 (RanB2) promotes the selective degradation of a subset of substrates of the ubiquitin-proteosme system (UPS), and the CLD may contribute to the compartmentalization of the UPS and the expressivity of neurological diseases.

the Ran-binding protein-1 cyclophilin domain promotes selectively the degradation of a subset of ubiquitin-proteosome system substrates and modulates the levels of RanGTPase activating protein and retinitus pigmentosa GTP-binding protein interacting protein-1a.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of RanBP2 in the regulation of protein homeostasis.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of the UPS activity.
the identification and characterization of the molecular determinants that regulate the activity of the UPS, which is essential for the maintenance of proteome homeostasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CLD of the RanBP2/Nup 358 protein is a selective modulator of the proteasome activity in vivo.
the CLD of the RanBP2 modulates selectively the UPS activity in vivo.
RanBP2 is an auxiliary regulator of the UPS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RanBP2 CLD modulates selectively the activity of the UPS, but not the proteasome itself.

the cyclophilin like domain (CLD), a conserved protein domain of the Ran binding protein 2 (RanBp2) interacts with the 19S regulatory complex of the proteasome, and that this domain modulates selectively the activity of the UPS.
the CLD of the RanBP2 protein modulates selectively the activity of the UPS in cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cyclophilin domain of Ran-binding protein 2, a nuclear pore component, modulates selectively the activity of the ubiquitin-protease system and protein biogenesis.

the cyclophilin (Cyp)-like domain (CLD), a domain that is present in a number of proteins, can act as a novel regulator of the UPS, and this may contribute to the modulation of the expressiveness of a number of neurological diseases.

the cyclophilin domain of Ran-binding protein 2 (RanBp2), an abundant nuclear protein, acts as an auxiliary modulator of protein degradation in a manner that is selective for a subset of proteins, including the ubiquitin-fusion degradation substrate ubiquitin-G76V-yellow fluorescent protein and the N-end-rule degradation substrate ubiquitin-arginine-yellow fluorescent protein.
